title: Momentum Reserve Autoscaler + Isolation Fence Playbook (PRD Draft)
content:
Purpose: capture a concrete, operationally realistic design for handling sudden demand surges on Dedicated pools while preserving isolation guarantees and predictable unit economics. This doc proposes the ‘Momentum Reserve’ concept (a lightweight, credit-based surge buffer) plus an Isolation Fence subsystem (soft admission controls + graceful degrade lanes) and an autoscaler that uses both short-horizon momentum signals and longer-horizon demand forecasts.

Context / why different: we already explored many reserve/burst variants. Momentum Reserve emphasizes low-friction, credit-encoded short-term capacity that decays quickly, paired with explicit fence policies that let us trade cost vs. isolation per-customer. The goal is a small, operational surface that product, infra, and SRE can test in the next quarter.

High-level goals (measurable):
- Keep 99.9th percentile tail latency within SLO for premium lanes in 95% of surge events (measured over rolling 30-day windows).
- Limit additional surge spend to <15% of baseline Dedicated spend for participating tenants on average per month.
- Avoid cross-tenant SLA violations in 99.95% of scheduling decisions (no noisy neighbor cross-impact above baseline).
- Provide clear per-tenant observability: momentum credits consumed, fence hits, degraded-route counts.

User stories and personas:
- Platform engineer: "We want transient surge smoothing so customers don’t get evicted during short spikes but don’t pay for long-term overprovision."
- SRE on customer side: "I need isolation fences so a coworker’s batch job won’t push my latency over SLO."
- Customer admin: "I want a configurable surge budget with an opt-in whitelist for costs and a dashboard to visualize credit usage."

Key concepts / terminology (new):
- Momentum Reserve (MR): a per-tenant short-duration credit pool (expressed in GPU-seconds-equivalent) that can be drawn to serve transient load beyond committed capacity. Credits have a half-life (default 30m) and monthly replenishment options.
- Isolation Fence: policy gates applied to scheduling decisions that prevent low-priority work from entering premium lanes; fences can be soft (throttle + degrade) or hard (reject).
- Latency Budget Tokens (LBT): a lightweight token representing a tenant’s allowed extra latency budget; consumed before MR to prefer preserving throughput.
- Replenish Modes: manual, timebox (daily/weekly), or usage-tied (top-up on billing event).

Design: components and flow
1) Telemetry intake: short-window metrics (1s, 10s, 1m) and demand forecast signals (5m, 30m) feed the autoscaler. Events tagged with route/model/fidelity.
2) MR allocator: per-tenant MR is tracked in the ledger (credit balance, decay rate, max cap). On an incoming request exceeding committed capacity, scheduler consults MR and LBT to decide immediate placement.
3) Isolation fence evaluator: concurrently evaluates policy rules (priority, affinity, model fingerprint) to determine allowed lanes. If fence would be violated, scheduler attempts one of: a) soft degrade (reduce fidelity), b) move to best-effort pool, c) reject with suggested retry.
4) Autoscaler kernel: two-layer control:
   - Short-horizon (momentum) controller: responsive to 1–5 minute momentum in requests; triggers hot-standby slices and temporary MR top-ups for participating tenants. Fast but bounded (max 10% of pool capacity).
   - Medium-horizon controller: uses 30m–6h forecasts to provision additional nodes into the pool or to kick off warm-prewarming pipelines. This controller respects min-cost constraints.
5) Cost & billing adapter: MR usage converted into line-items (credits consumed, soft-fidelity downgrade discounts) visible in billing. Customers can opt to auto-topup with billing triggers.

Scheduler decision matrix (simplified):
- If tenant within committed capacity -> normal placement.
- If overcommitted AND Isolation Fence allows AND MR >= request_cost -> draw MR and place into premium or hot path (respecting per-tenant throttle).
- If overcommitted AND Fence denies premium path -> try degraded fidelity lane (if allowed) -> else route to best-effort -> else return explicit 429 with suggested backoff and link to MR purchase.

APIs / UX:
- Customer API: GET /dedicated/tenants/{id}/momentum-status -> balance, decay, history; POST /dedicated/tenants/{id}/momentum-topup -> purchase topup.
- Console: new ‘Momentum’ card on tenant detail with sparkline of credits, fence violations, and predicted exhaustion time at current burn.
- Alerting: default alert when MR projected to zero within 10 minutes for any active premium route (severity P2).

Observability & metrics (minimum):
- MR_balance_gse (gse = GPU-seconds equivalent) per tenant (gauge).
- MR_consumption_rate{tenant,route} (rate).
- Fence_denied_requests_total{tenant,reason}.
- Degraded_route_count and Degraded_request_latency_percentiles.
- Cost_delta_per_tenant_due_to_MR (monthly).

Operational playbook (runbook excerpts):
- If premium SLO breaches during surge: check top tenants consuming MR -> evaluate whether to temporarily increase MR cap for affected tenants (manual override) or enforce stricter fences.
- MR exhaustion during sustained surge: recommend migrating high-volume background jobs to scheduled off-peak windows; ops can enable temporary rate-limits via fence policies.
- Suspicious consumption pattern: flag for fraud/noise if MR consumption spikes > 10x median in 1h and correlated with >50% of requests coming from a single route.

Safety & guardrails:
- MR per-request cap: limit how many credits a single request can burn (default 2x of typical request cost) to avoid blowouts.
- Pool-level surge cap: system-level ceiling on MR-driven hot allocation (e.g., 15% of pool) to avoid unbounded spillover.
- Decay enforcement: credits older than 48h without activity expire to avoid stale liabilities.

Economics and pricing model sketch:
- Baseline: MR included at a small monthly stipend for all Dedicated customers with bigger stipends for enterprise tiers.
- Top-ups: pay-as-you-go per GPU-second with volume discounts.
- Fidelity downgrades: when using degraded lanes customers get a per-token discount (visible on billing) to signal quality tradeoff.

Experiment plan (Q1):
- Phase A (canary, internal): launch MR for 5 internal tenants and two synthetic tenants simulating 3x spikes. Validate tail latency and cost leakage.
- Phase B (early customers): invite 8 existing Dedicated customers (mix of mid-market and enterprise) with opt-in MR topups and dashboard. Collect UX feedback for console and API.
- Phase C (wider): enable auto-topup and integrate with billing; tune defaults.

Success metrics for experiments:
- 75% reduction in evictions during 5–15 minute spikes for opted-in customers.
- Median cost-per-spike for MR usage < projected baseline reservation cost.
- Customer-reported satisfaction >= 4/5 on isolated-surges questionnaire.

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- Default decay half-life: 30m vs 60m (sensitivity to transient bursts vs sustained).
- Visibility: what minimum telemetry window we require for MR decisions without increasing ingestion costs.
- How to price fidelity downgrades (flat % vs per-token dynamic).
- Integration surface with Private deployments (on-prem): MR ledger can be hosted in customer control plane or centrally — what are compliance implications?

Implementation milestones (rough):
1) MR ledger prototype + small simulator (2 weeks)
2) Short-horizon autoscaler + scheduler hooks + console prototype (4 weeks)
3) Fence rule engine + policy DSL + runbook draft (3 weeks)
4) Billing adapter + topup API + canary (3 weeks)
5) Early customer beta + feedback loop (6 weeks)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: MR misconfiguration allows runaway spend. Mitigation: conservative defaults, hard caps, mandatory billing alerts at 50% projected spend.
- Risk: Increased scheduler complexity. Mitigation: keep MR decision path as a fast-path pre-check; fallback to existing scheduling if MR path fails.

Appendix: quick simulation notes (for infra team)
- Synthetic traffic generator: mix of short chat requests (p95 tokens small) and long text-gen tails. Inject 90s spike windows every 20m.
- Success baseline: system should absorb spikes by consuming MR without >10% increase in aggregate latency for non-participating tenants.

Notes / todos:
- Follow up with billing on topup UX: @Luca (JIRA-DED-1817).
- Schedule architecture review with serving-runtime and infra next Thurs.
- Create small prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sim/momentum-allocator.

-- end of draft --

This doc is intentionally pragmatic and short-form; it is a working PRD to collect early feedback before expanding to fuller design docs and engineering tickets.
